You are building one of two test-corpus apps for `entire graph`, a Go code-graph provider (repo: /Users/abhi/Documents/entire-graph, branch `vue-corpus`, already checked out). Today `.vue` files are "inventory-only": the provider emits a `component` and a `document` symbol per `.vue` file (name = file basename, spanning the whole file, starting line 1) plus an `element` symbol per HTML `id="..."`, and never parses `<script>` blocks. `.ts`/`.js` files are fully parsed (functions, nested functions with CONTAINS, classes, CALLS, IMPORTS with relative/extensionless resolution, DATA_FLOWS, EMITS/LISTENS_ON to `external:channel:<name>` for `bus.emit("x")`/`bus.on("x")` patterns). The corpus measures how much of a correct Vue graph the provider emits, so future Vue work can be scored.

## Read first
- `internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/README.md`: the corpus spec: manifest format and the tag list. Follow it exactly.
- `internal/sem/vue_corpus_test.go`: exactly how facts are self-checked (`TestVueCorpusManifestMatchesSource`) and scored (`TestVueCorpusScore`). Do not edit this file or the README. If you think either is wrong, say so in your final report instead.

## Your app: `internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/helpdesk/`
A realistic Vue 2.7-style Options API + plain JavaScript customer-support helpdesk ("helpdesk"): tickets, ticket list with filters and pagination, ticket detail with replies, customers, agents, canned responses, SLA timers, notifications, reports. This is the legacy enterprise dialect, the opposite of `<script setup>`. Aim for roughly 40 source files (`.vue` + `.js`) plus `package.json`, `jsconfig.json` (with `"paths": {"@/*": ["src/*"]}`), `vue.config.js` (webpack alias `@` -> `src`), and `public/index.html`. Write code a Vue 2 developer would recognise as normal; it is never built or run. No `node_modules`, no lockfiles, ASCII only, LF line endings. Every relative and `@/` import must point at a file that exists in the app (externals like `vue`, `vuex`, `vue-router`, `axios`, `@vue/test-utils`, `jest` are fine).

Cover these constructs, each in several places, so every relevant tag gets at least ~5 facts:
- `<script>` blocks with `export default { name, components: {...}, props: {... with type/default/validator}, data() {...}, computed: {...}, watch: { x: { handler() {}, deep: true } }, created() {}, mounted() {}, beforeDestroy() {}, methods: {...} }`. Methods call each other via `this.otherMethod()` and call imported helpers.
- Local registration with kebab-case template use (`components: { TicketRow }` used as `<ticket-row>`), and global registration in `src/main.js` (`Vue.component('base-button', BaseButton)`, a second global) used elsewhere without importing.
- Vuex in `src/store/index.js` with namespaced modules in `src/store/modules/*.js` (state, getters, mutations as `SET_TICKETS(state, x)`, actions as `async fetchTickets({ commit }, params)` that call an API layer and `commit('SET_TICKETS', ...)`). Components use `this.$store.dispatch('tickets/fetchTickets', ...)`, `this.$store.commit(...)`, `mapState`, `mapGetters`, and `mapActions(['tickets/...'])` / `mapActions('tickets', ['fetchTickets'])` followed by `this.fetchTickets()`.
- Mixins in `src/mixins/` (e.g. `paginationMixin`, `slaTimerMixin`, `formValidationMixin`) exported as objects with `data`, `methods`, and lifecycle hooks; components list them in `mixins: [...]` and call mixin methods via `this.nextPage()`. Use `extends: BaseListView` in at least one component.
- An event bus in `src/eventBus.js` (`export const EventBus = new Vue()`) with `EventBus.$emit('ticket:assigned', ...)` in several places and `EventBus.$on('ticket:assigned', this.onAssigned)` / `$off` in others; component custom events via `this.$emit('reply-sent', reply)` with the parent listening through `@reply-sent="onReplySent"` / `v-on:reply-sent`.
- vue-router in `src/router/index.js` with lazy routes (`component: () => import('@/views/TicketDetail.vue')`), a `beforeEach` guard calling a store getter, and `this.$router.push(...)` in components.
- At least one `.vue` file with `<script src="./TicketTimer.js"></script>` pointing at an external script file, and one with a `<template lang="pug">` or a `functional` template, to test non-default blocks.
- Filters or plain helper modules in `src/utils/` (date formatting, SLA math, priority mapping) imported both by components and by store modules.
- An API layer in `src/api/` (`http.js` wrapping axios, plus resource modules) called from store actions.
- Templates with `@click="fn"`, `v-on:submit.prevent="fn"`, `v-model`, `v-for`, `slot`/`slot-scope` or `v-slot`, and child tags in kebab-case.
- HTML-id traps for `absent_symbols`: attributes like `:ticket-id="currentTicketId"`, `data-id="row"`, `v-bind:id="rowDomId"`, `:id="inputId"`, `aria-labelledby` style attributes ending in `id=`. Each trap value must NOT be a real static `id`. Also include a few real static ids (`id="ticket-list"`) and list those as `baseline` element symbols.
- Tests: `tests/unit/*.spec.js` (jest + `@vue/test-utils`) that import and exercise a store module, a mixin, a util, and a component (`shallowMount(TicketRow, ...)`).

## Manifest: `helpdesk/expected.json`
Aim for 200 to 300 facts. Rules:
- List every `.vue` file's `component` symbol (`"kind": "component"`, `"line": 1`, tag `baseline`), plus the static HTML ids, plus the important `.js` symbols, as `baseline` facts.
- Every symbol a relation names must also be listed in `symbols` (the self-check enforces this).
- Give each fact the single most specific tag: the capability that must exist before a correct provider could emit it. Examples: a `methods:` entry, `computed` property, `watch` handler or lifecycle hook in a `.vue` file is `options-api`; `this.helper()` between two methods is `options-api`; a method's call to an imported util is `script-calls`; `import X from '@/...'` from a `.vue` file is `path-alias` (from a plain `.js` file also `path-alias` if it does not resolve today); a relative import from a `.vue` file is `script-imports`; `this.$store.dispatch('tickets/fetchTickets')` -> CALLS to the `fetchTickets` action is `store-members`, and so are `commit('SET_TICKETS')` -> the mutation and `mapActions` + `this.fetchTickets()`; a component using a mixin is `mixins` (type `["INHERITS","EXTENDS"]` from the component to the mixin object symbol) and `this.nextPage()` -> the mixin method is `mixins`; `EventBus.$emit('ticket:assigned')` is EMITS to `{"external": "ticket:assigned"}` and `$on` is LISTENS_ON, tagged `event-bus` (and `this.$emit('reply-sent')` plus the parent's `@reply-sent` the same way); `Vue.component('base-button', BaseButton)` used as `<base-button>` in another component is `global-registration` (type `["CALLS","ACCESSES"]` from the user component to the BaseButton component); `<ticket-row>` rendered by `TicketList` or `@click="assign"` handled by `assign` is `template-edges`; `() => import('@/views/X.vue')` is `lazy-imports` (IMPORTS from the router file to the view file); `<script src>` is `script-src`; a spec covering a target is `tests` (type `TESTS`).
- Leave out `kind` on script symbols unless the distinction matters (`class`, `component`); a future implementation may label an Options API method `method` or `function`.
- `baseline` means the provider emits it TODAY. Verify that: run `VUE_CORPUS_VERBOSE=1 go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpusScore' -v -count=1` from the repo root. It will fail because `score.json` does not exist yet and possibly because the other app (`taskboard`, built in parallel by someone else) is missing or incomplete; ignore those failures and ignore taskboard entirely. Read the `helpdesk: N baseline facts are not emitted` error and the per-tag missing lists. Any fact you tagged `baseline` that is missing must be retagged (if it is a real gap, such as a Vuex action defined as an object-literal method in a `.js` module, use the matching tag like `store-members`) or fixed in the manifest if you got the line or name wrong. Facts under other tags may be found today; that is fine, keep their tag, but mention notable ones in your report.
- Run `go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpusManifestMatchesSource/helpdesk' -v -count=1` until it passes.

## Constraints
- Only create files under `internal/sem/testdata/vuecorpus/helpdesk/`. Do not create `score.json`, do not touch other paths, do not commit, do not run `-update`.
- The first `go test` in `internal/sem` compiles CGO grammars and may take a few minutes; later runs are faster. Run commands directly (macOS has no `timeout`).

## Final report (under 300 words)
File count, fact count per tag, the TODAY score per tag from the last test run, any facts outside `baseline` that the provider already emits, any surprising provider behavior you noticed (for example whether Vuex object-literal actions in `.js` files become symbols), and any concern about the spec or harness.

<system-reminder>
Your final report is delivered through SubagentHandback: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so make it your last step. Only a SubagentHandback call reaches your caller as your result; plain text you write at the end is not delivered. Do not also send the report with SendMessage: your caller would get it twice.
</system-reminder>

# Vue Corpus

Two realistic Vue applications with a hand-written ground truth. Each app has an
`expected.json` that lists the symbols and relations a correct graph contains,
and tags every fact with the gap it measures. `vue_corpus_test.go` builds a
snapshot of each app, scores it against `expected.json`, and ratchets the
result in `score.json`, so every Vue improvement shows up as facts gained per
tag and every regression fails the test.

```sh
go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpus' -v            # score and compare
go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpusScore' -update  # record a new score
VUE_CORPUS_VERBOSE=1 go test ./internal/sem -run 'TestVueCorpusScore' -v  # list every missing fact
```

| App | Dialect |
|---|---|
| `taskboard/` | Vue 3, TypeScript, `<script setup lang="ts">`, Pinia, vue-router, composables, `@/` path alias |
| `helpdesk/` | Options API, JavaScript, Vuex modules, mixins, event bus, global registration, kebab-case tags |

The apps are never built or run. They contain no `node_modules` or lockfiles,
and every relative and aliased import resolves to a file in the app.

## Manifest Format

```json
{
  "app": "taskboard",
  "symbols": [
    {"file": "src/components/TaskCard.vue", "name": "toggleDone", "kind": "function", "line": 31, "tag": "script-symbols"}
  ],
  "absent_symbols": [
    {"file": "src/App.vue", "name": "selectedId", "tag": "false-elements", "why": ":task-id=\"selectedId\" is a prop binding, not an HTML id"}
  ],
  "relations": [
    {"type": "IMPORTS", "from": {"file": "src/App.vue"}, "to": {"file": "src/stores/tasks.ts"}, "tag": "script-imports"},
    {"type": "CALLS", "from": {"file": "src/components/TaskCard.vue", "name": "toggleDone"}, "to": {"file": "src/stores/tasks.ts", "name": "toggleTask"}, "tag": "store-members"},
    {"type": ["CALLS", "ACCESSES"], "from": {"file": "src/views/BoardView.vue", "name": "BoardView", "kind": "component"}, "to": {"file": "src/components/TaskCard.vue", "name": "TaskCard", "kind": "component"}, "tag": "template-edges"}
  ]
}
```

- `symbols[].line` is the line that declares the name. A symbol matches when a
  snapshot symbol in that file has the same name, the same kind if `kind` is
  given, and a range that contains `line`.
- `absent_symbols` lists symbols a correct graph must not emit. The name must
  appear in the file, so the trap is real.
- A relation endpoint is a file (`file` only), a symbol (`file` and `name`,
  optionally `kind`), or an external package (`external`, such as `"pinia"`).
  `type` is one relation type or a list of acceptable types.
- Every named endpoint also appears in `symbols`, so the manifest checks itself.

## Tags

Each tag maps to a gap in the Vue gap analysis (G1 to G8) or to a construct the
analysis did not cover yet.

| Tag | Gap | What it measures |
|---|---|---|
| `baseline` | | Facts the provider emits today: plain `.ts`/`.js` code, `.vue` component symbols, static HTML ids. The test fails if any is missing. |
| `script-symbols` | G2 | Functions, consts, and classes declared in `<script>` or `<script setup>` |
| `script-imports` | G3 | IMPORTS from a `.vue` file to `.ts`, `.js`, or `.vue` files |
| `script-calls` | G3 | CALLS from a script function to an imported function |
| `component-owner` | G4 | CONTAINS from the component to its script symbols, and top-level setup calls attributed to the component |
| `false-elements` | G5 | HTML-id false positives that must not appear |
| `template-edges` | G6 | Template event handlers to script functions, and component tags to the component they render |
| `options-api` | G7 | `methods`, `computed`, `watch`, and lifecycle hooks as symbols |
| `store-members` | G8 | Calls through store instances, destructured members, Pinia actions, and Vuex `dispatch`/`commit` strings |
| `path-alias` | new | `@/` imports resolved through the `tsconfig.json` or bundler alias |
| `lazy-imports` | new | `() => import('./X.vue')` routes and `defineAsyncComponent` |
| `global-registration` | new | `app.component` / `Vue.component` registrations used as tags elsewhere |
| `ts-types` | new | Types from `.ts` files used in `.vue` files (`defineProps<Props>()`, typed refs, typed params) |
| `mixins` | new | Components that use a mixin, and calls to mixin members through `this` |
| `event-bus` | new | EMITS and LISTENS_ON for event-bus channels and component custom events (`emit('x')` with `@x=` in the parent) |
| `tests` | new | TESTS from spec files to the composables, stores, and components they cover |
| `script-src` | new | `<script src="./x.js">` external script blocks |

name: graph-plugin-v040-use-built-binary
description: "Installed `entire graph` v0.4.0 lacks `query` and its --head search hangs on this repo; build from main and use that binary for Graph lookups"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: a1870155-101a-49bb-a35b-e3e8ed3d1416
  modified: 2026-10-21T16:11:46.716Z
---

As of 2026-10-21 the installed `entire graph` plugin is v0.4.0. It has no `query` command (`unknown command "query"`; it calls it `search`), and `entire graph search --repo . --profile full --head ...` ran 10+ minutes on this repo without finishing (killed). It predates the records-cache spool fix (#349).

A binary built from main works for every Graph lookup AGENTS.md requires: `go build -o /tmp/eg-before ./cmd/entire-graph`, then `/tmp/eg-before query|def|neighbors|impact --repo . --head ...`. Cold index ~20s, warm calls <1s.

**Why:** AGENTS.md mandates Graph `query/def/neighbors/impact --head` for every locate question; with the stale plugin that mandate stalls the session.

**How to apply:** At session start, run `entire graph version`; if it is still v0.4.0 (or `query` is missing), build from main and use that binary for Graph calls, and say so in the report. Recheck once the plugin is upgraded; delete this memory when the installed plugin has `query`.

content.content:
Export the whole graph: files, symbols, and relations

Usage:
  entire graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson|compact-ndjson|scip [--worktree]

One header record, then file, external-endpoint, symbol, and relation records. Native and compact NDJSON stream so memory stays bounded; the experimental scip format assembles one complete protobuf Index in memory. The snapshot is a superset of symbols + edges + files for ingestion into agent memory or a store such as Entire Brain. compact-ndjson can be read by snapshot-query. scip reserves stderr for one machine-readable omission note and cannot be combined with --progress.

Flags:
  --repo <path>           Repository (default: current repo)
  --format ndjson|compact-ndjson|scip
                          Output format; compact and scip require a complete snapshot (default: ndjson)
  --worktree              Stream the working tree instead of HEAD (never cached)
  --progress              Emit progress events to stderr
  --profile syntax-only|fast|full
                          Parsing depth (default: full)
  --ignore-file <path>    Extra gitignore-style exclude rules (repeatable)
  --include-file <path>   Re-include ignored paths (gitignore-style; not an allowlist)

Examples:
  entire graph snapshot --repo . --format ndjson
  entire graph snapshot --repo . --format compact-ndjson > graph.compact.ndjson
  entire graph snapshot --repo . --format scip > index.scip

<template>
  <form id="ticket-filters" class="ticket-filters" v-on:submit.prevent="apply">
    <label for="filter-status">Status</label>
    <select id="filter-status" v-model="local.status">
      <option v-for="option in statusOptions" :key="option.value" :value="option.value">
        {{ option.label }}
      </option>
    </select>
    <label :for="priorityInputId">Priority</label>
    <select :id="priorityInputId" v-model="local.priority">
      <option value="">Any</option>
      <option v-for="priority in priorities" :key="priority" :value="priority">
        {{ priority | priority }}
      </option>
    </select>
    <input
      id="filter-query"
      v-model.trim="local.query"
      type="search"
      placeholder="Search subject or customer"
      @keyup.esc="reset"
    >
    <base-button type="submit" :disabled="!isDirty">Apply</base-button>
    <base-button variant="link" @click="reset">Reset</base-button>
  </form>
</template>

<script>
import { PRIORITIES } from '../../utils/priority'

const DEFAULT_FILTERS = {
  status: 'open',
  priority: '',
  assignee: '',
  query: ''
}

export default {
  name: 'TicketFilters',
  props: {
    value: {
      type: Object,
      required: true
    }
  },
  data() {
    return {
      local: Object.assign({}, this.value),
      priorities: PRIORITIES,
      statusOptions: [
        { value: 'open', label: 'Open' },
        { value: 'pending', label: 'Pending' },
        { value: 'solved', label: 'Solved' },
        { value: 'closed', label: 'Closed' }
      ]
    }
  },
  computed: {
    priorityInputId() {
      return 'filter-priority-' + this._uid
    },
    isDirty() {
      return JSON.stringify(this.local) !== JSON.stringify(this.value)
    }
  },
  watch: {
    value: {
      handler(next) {
        this.local = Object.assign({}, next)
      },
      deep: true
    }
  },
  methods: {
    apply() {
      this.$emit('change', Object.assign({}, this.local))
    },
    reset() {
      this.local = Object.assign({}, DEFAULT_FILTERS)
      this.apply()
    }
  }
}
</script>

}
